compute.note: The chips that turn energy into inference and training.

memory.note: The memory bandwidth that feeds the chips; often the binding limit.

packaging.note: Foundry processes and advanced packaging that turn designs into parts.

data-centres.note: Buildings that hold the compute, measured in power drawn rather than square metres.
indicators: LBNL, United States Data Center Energy Usage Report

generation.note: New power — and the price of firm capacity when it runs short.
indicators: PJM Interconnection, Base Residual Auction results

grid.note: Wires, interconnection queues and storage between generation and load.
indicators: EIA, Electric Power Annual and Monthly

cooling.note: Heat removal, from the chip stack to the building.

power-electronics.note: Converters and drives that move power into chips and machines.

robotics.note: Machines that act: actuators, arms and the learning that drives them.
indicators: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics

sensing.note: Cameras, depth sensors and lidar: how machines perceive.
